# @vantreeseba/graphql-casl

> A [`graphql-middleware`](https://github.com/dimagi/graphql-middleware) plugin for defining [CASL](https://casl.js.org/) permission rules that apply to GraphQL resolvers. Declare rules per type/field in a `PermissionsMap`; each rule runs before the underlying resolver and throws if the request is not allowed. The library is **schema-agnostic** — subject names and condition types are derived from your own generated `Resolvers` / `ResolversTypes`, so there is no manual type listing.

## Install

```bash
npm install @vantreeseba/graphql-casl
# peer deps
npm install @casl/ability graphql graphql-middleware
```

Requires `@casl/ability >=6`, `graphql >=16`, and `graphql-middleware >=6` as peer dependencies. `@envelop/core >=5` and `@envelop/on-resolve >=7` are **optional** peer dependencies, installed only by consumers who import the `/envelop` entry point. TypeScript 5, ESM only. No runtime dependencies.

One optional sibling package, `@vantreeseba/graphql-casl-codegen` (a GraphQL Code Generator plugin that emits the subject bindings), plus two optional entry points on the runtime itself: `@vantreeseba/graphql-casl/scoping` (rewrites a field's filter argument instead of allowing or denying it) and `@vantreeseba/graphql-casl/envelop` (enforces the same map through envelop instead of `graphql-middleware`).

## Public API

All exports come from `@vantreeseba/graphql-casl` (re-exported through `src/index.ts`).

| Export | What it does |
|---|---|
| `createGraphQLAbility<SubjectMap>()` | Returns a CASL `AbilityBuilder` typed against your schema — `can`/`cannot` conditions are checked against each subject's fields — with `__typename` subject detection applied by `build()`. |
| `buildGraphQLAbility<SubjectMap>(rules, options?)` | Rebuilds an ability from stored `GraphQLRule`s (e.g. rules persisted in a database). |
| `createCan(getAbility, isAuthenticated, buildSubject?, options?)` | Factory returning a `requireCan(action, subject, getSubjectData?)` rule builder, bound to your context shape and ability builder. `getAbility(context)` is memoized per request. |
| `requireCan.onResult(action, subject, getSubjectData?)` | Post-execution rule: runs the resolver and checks the ability against the value it returned. Refuses root mutation fields before resolving. |
| `requireCan.fields(action, subject)` | One rule for a whole type; decides each field with `ability.can(action, subject, info.fieldName)`. |
| `createTyped<SubjectMap>()` | Returns a `typed(type, attrs)` helper that tags plain objects with `__typename` for CASL's runtime subject detection. |
| `createSubjects<SubjectMap>()` | Validates a subject-name const object against your schema's domain types. |
| `rule(check, opts?)` | Wraps a predicate `(parent, args, ctx, info) => boolean \| string \| Error` into a combinable rule. |
| `and` / `or` / `not` / `chain` / `race` | Combinators over combinable rules. `and`/`or` evaluate in parallel; `chain`/`race` short-circuit. A rule that needs the resolver to decide is rejected as an operand when the map is built. |
| `wrap(...rules)` | Nests any rules as middleware — each receives the next as its `resolve`, outermost first. The escape hatch for rules the combinators reject (`onResult`, `scopeArgs`, hand-written middleware). Returns a plain `Rule`, so it is never itself a combinator operand. |
| `accept` / `deny` | Always-pass / always-fail rule primitives; both are combinable. |
| `isCheckableRule(value)` | Whether a rule can be a combinator operand. |
| `applyPermissions(schema, permissions, options?)` | Validates the map against the runtime schema and applies it via `applyMiddleware`. Options: `fallbackRule`, `fallbackError`, `allowExternalErrors`, `debug`, `maskDenials`. |
| `resolvePermissions(schema, permissions, options?)` | The same layer without the `graphql-middleware` binding: a memoized `(typeName, fieldName) => Rule \| undefined` lookup for building another integration. |
| `PermissionsError` | Thrown when the map names a type or field the schema lacks; aggregates every problem. |
| `accessibleBy(ability, action, subject, adapter?)` | Folds the ability's rules into a query filter for row-level filtering. `null` means deny-all; `{}` means no restriction. |
| `scopeArgs(requireCan, action, subject, options)` | **Subpath export `@vantreeseba/graphql-casl/scoping`.** A rule that rewrites a field's filter argument (`into`, default `'where'`) with the ability's filter instead of allowing or denying the field — for generated CRUD resolvers you cannot edit. Not combinable; compose it with `wrap`. |
| `useGraphQLCasl<Resolvers>(options)` | **Subpath export `@vantreeseba/graphql-casl/envelop`.** An envelop `Plugin` that enforces the same `PermissionsMap` by wrapping resolvers as envelop hands them over, instead of wrapping the schema with `graphql-middleware`. `options.permissions` is the map; every other key is an `ApplyPermissionsOptions` field. |
| `Actions` | Const map of `create` / `read` / `update` / `delete` / `manage`. |

Type helpers: `PermissionsMap`, `Rule`, `CheckableRule`, `Check`, `RuleResult`, `Wildcard`, `RequireCan`, `RequireCanBare`, `RequireCanFields`, `RequireCanOnResult`, `BuildSubject`, `CreateCanOptions`, `UnconditionedSubjectMode`, `SubjectName`, `SubjectMap`, `ArgsOf`, `ParentOf`, `ContextOf`, `Action`, `AbilityLike`, `GraphQLAbility`, `GraphQLAbilities`, `GraphQLRule`, `GraphQLAbilityOptions`, `ApplyPermissionsOptions`, `FallbackError`, `PermissionResolver`, `AccessibleFilter`, `FilterAdapter` (`SkeletonAdapter` | `LeafAdapter`), `AdapterCore`, `LeafCondition`, `LeafOperator`. From `/scoping`: `ScopeOptions`, `OnDenyAll`, `Scopable`. From `/envelop`: `GraphQLCaslPluginOptions`.

A failed authentication check throws `Not authenticated`; a failed ability check throws `Forbidden`, or the matched rule's `cannot(...).because('...')` reason.

## Usage

### 1. Build abilities

```ts
import {
  Actions,
  createGraphQLAbility,
  createSubjects,
  createTyped,
  type GraphQLAbility,
  type SubjectMap,
} from '@vantreeseba/graphql-casl';
import type { Resolvers, ResolversTypes } from './__generated__/resolvers.js';

type AppSubjectMap = SubjectMap<Resolvers, ResolversTypes>;
type AppAbility = GraphQLAbility<AppSubjectMap>;

export const typed = createTyped<AppSubjectMap>();
export const Subject = createSubjects<AppSubjectMap>()({
  User: 'User',
  Note: 'Note',
} as const);

export function defineAbilitiesFor(userId: string | undefined): AppAbility {
  const { can, cannot, build } = createGraphQLAbility<AppSubjectMap>();
  if (!userId) {
    cannot(Actions.manage, 'all');
    return build();
  }
  can(Actions.read, Subject.Note);
  can(Actions.update, Subject.Note, { userId }); // condition on the subject's fields
  can(Actions.read, Subject.Note, { status: { $in: ['draft', 'live'] } });
  return build();
}
```

Conditions are CASL mongo-query operators (`$eq`, `$ne`, `$in`, `$nin`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$lt`, `$lte`, …) and are plain JSON, so rules can be stored in a database and rehydrated with `buildGraphQLAbility`.

### 2. Bind `createCan` to your context

```ts
import { createCan } from '@vantreeseba/graphql-casl';
import type { Context } from './context.js';
import { defineAbilitiesFor, typed } from './abilities.js';

const canUser = createCan<Context, AppSubjectMap>(
  async (ctx) => defineAbilitiesFor(ctx.userId),
  (ctx) => ctx.userId != null,
  typed,
);
```

### 3. Declare the permissions map

`getSubjectData` pulls condition values out of the resolver args (and optionally the parent); without it the rule checks against the bare subject type.

```ts
import { accept, and, deny, rule, type PermissionsMap } from '@vantreeseba/graphql-casl';
import type { Resolvers, MutationUpdateNotesArgs } from './__generated__/resolvers.js';

const isNotBanned = rule((_parent, _args, ctx: Context) => !ctx.user?.banned || 'Account suspended');

export const permissions: PermissionsMap<Resolvers> = {
  Query: {
    // onResult authorizes the Note the resolver actually loaded, not args.id
    note: canUser.onResult(Actions.read, Subject.Note),
    me: canUser(Actions.read, Subject.User),
  },
  Mutation: {
    requestMagicLink: accept, // public
    deleteNotes: deny,        // nobody, ever
    updateNotes: and(
      isNotBanned,
      canUser<MutationUpdateNotesArgs>(Actions.update, Subject.Note, (args) => ({
        userId: args.where?.userId?.eq,
      })),
    ),
  },
  // one rule for the whole type; each field is decided by the ability's field list
  Note: { '*': canUser.fields(Actions.read, Subject.Note) },
};
```

`'*'` works as a type key and as a field key. Precedence, highest first: a named field of a named type, any field of a named type, a named field of any type, any field of any type, then `fallbackRule`. Wildcards never compose — exactly one rule guards a field.

### 4. Apply to the schema

```ts
import { applyPermissions, deny } from '@vantreeseba/graphql-casl';

const schemaWithPermissions = applyPermissions<Resolvers>(schema, permissions, {
  fallbackRule: deny,  // deny-by-default across the whole schema
  maskDenials: true,   // resolve a denied field to null/[] instead of throwing
});
```

The map is validated against the runtime schema: a rule on a type or field the schema lacks throws `PermissionsError` naming every problem. Introspection types are never guarded.

### 5. Row-level filtering (optional)

```ts
import { accessibleBy, Actions } from '@vantreeseba/graphql-casl';

const filter = accessibleBy(await ctx.ability, Actions.read, 'Note');
if (filter === null) return []; // nothing is accessible
return db.notes.find(filter);
```

A `FilterAdapter` swaps the dialect. One with `rule(conditions, inverted)` replaces only the boolean skeleton and passes conditions through as written; one with `leaf(condition)` + `not(filter)` also receives each comparison individually (`{ path, operator, value }`, dotted keys already split), so a dialect that spells equality differently does not have to walk the conditions itself. An operator a leaf adapter cannot express must throw — dropping a clause would widen access.

### 6. Scoping generated resolvers (optional)

```ts
import { scopeArgs } from '@vantreeseba/graphql-casl/scoping';

const permissions = {
  Query: { notes: scopeArgs(canUser, Actions.read, 'Note', { adapter: drizzleFilters }) },
} satisfies PermissionsMap<Resolvers>;
```

Options: `adapter` (required), `into` (default `'where'`), `merge` (default `adapter.and([clientFilter, scope])`), `onDenyAll` (`'deny'` throws `Forbidden`, `'nothing'` injects `adapter.nothing()`). Caveats: a scoped field returns fewer rows rather than an error; injected arguments bypass GraphQL input coercion, so a wrong-dialect filter fails silently (`applyPermissions` at least checks that `into` names a real argument of the field); never merge by spreading keys, since a client `{ OR: [...] }` would escape the scope; pair it with `fallbackRule`, because scoping is not a gate, or put a gate in front of it with `wrap(isNotBanned, scoped)`. `wrap` also stacks scoping with `onResult`, which no combinator can express.

### 7. Enforcing the map through envelop (optional)

```ts
import { useGraphQLCasl } from '@vantreeseba/graphql-casl/envelop';

const yoga = createYoga({
  schema,
  plugins: [useGraphQLCasl<Resolvers>({ permissions, fallbackRule: deny, maskDenials: true })],
});
```

`applyPermissions` wraps a schema up front, which needs a schema you own and can replace — awkward on Apollo Server 4+, on federated gateways, and anywhere the schema is built or swapped for you. This plugin hooks resolvers as envelop hands them over, so the same map works wherever envelop does (Yoga, Apollo with the envelop integration, Hive Gateway, `graphql-ws`). It calls `resolvePermissions` rather than reimplementing anything, so wildcard precedence, `fallbackRule` coverage, error control and masking are identical. The map is validated when the schema arrives rather than on the first query that touches the offending field, and a schema swapped at runtime is re-validated; introspection is never guarded; a field with no resolver of its own is guarded too (the default resolver is wrapped, which is what makes `requireCan.fields(...)` work); each field is wrapped once however many times it resolves. Use this **or** `applyPermissions`, never both — two layers would run every rule twice.

## Key conventions

- The library is schema-agnostic: type helpers (`SubjectName`, `SubjectMap`, `ArgsOf`, `ParentOf`, `ContextOf`) are derived from the consumer's generated `Resolvers` / `ResolversTypes` — never hardcode domain type names.
- Runtime subject detection uses `__typename`, applied by `createGraphQLAbility().build()`, so consumers tag plain objects with `createTyped()` rather than CASL's `subject()`.
- `createCan` / `createSubjects` / `createTyped` are factories bound to the consumer's context shape and ability builder — keep auth/ability logic out of the library core.
- Only *denials* are masked or reworded. A rule that failed with a bug of its own and a resolver that failed on a permitted field both keep their own errors, so an outage is never reported as a permission decision.
- `allowExternalErrors` defaults to `true` — the opposite of `graphql-shield`, which masks resolver errors by default.

## Source modules

- `src/index.ts` — public API entry point (re-exports + package overview)
- `src/schemaTypes.ts` — type helpers derived from generated Resolvers/ResolversTypes
- `src/rules.ts` — the rule layer (`Rule`, `CheckableRule`, `PermissionsMap`, `rule`, `accept`, `deny`)
- `src/combinators.ts` — `and` / `or` / `not` / `chain` / `race`, plus `wrap`
- `src/applyPermissions.ts` — schema walk, wildcard precedence, error control, masking
- `src/accessibleBy.ts` — the ability-to-query-filter fold
- `src/conditions.ts` — the `FilterAdapter` union (skeleton/leaf) and the conditions walker
- `src/scoping.ts` — the optional `/scoping` entry point: `scopeArgs`
- `src/envelop.ts` — the optional `/envelop` entry point: `useGraphQLCasl`
- `src/internal.ts` — symbols shared between modules that must not import each other
- `src/ability.ts` — CASL `Action` / `Actions` / `AbilityLike`
- `src/graphqlAbility.ts` — `GraphQLAbility` / `createGraphQLAbility` / `buildGraphQLAbility`
- `src/subjects.ts` — `createSubjects` / `createTyped`
- `src/createCan.ts` — the factory tying a CASL ability to the rule layer
